questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 15% per annum is half of the compound interest on ₹5,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum. What is the sum placed on simple interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal invested on CI = ₹5000

Time = 2 year

Rate of Interest = 15% for SI and 10% for CI

**Formula used:**

**1**. SI = PRT / 100

**2**. CI = P[1 + (R/100)]ⁿT - P

Where, P = Principal, R = Rate, T = Time (in years)

n = Number of times interest compounded per year

**Calculation:**

CI = 5000 × [1 + (10/100)]²- 5000

questions.question: In a class of 45 students, the average age of the class is 18 years. The average age of 35 students is 15. What is the average age of the remaining 10 students?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of 45 students = 18 years

Average of 35 students = 15 years

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of ages of all students) / (Number of students)

**Calculation:**

The average age of 45 students = 18

⇒ Sum of ages of 45 students = 45 × 18 = 810

The average age of 35 students = 15

⇒ Sum of ages of 35 students = 35 × 15 = 525

Sum of ages of remaining 10 students = 810 - 525

⇒ Sum of ages of remaining 10 students = 285

Average age of remaining 10 students = 285/10

⇒ Average age of remaining 10 students = 28.5

**∴ The average**** age of the remaining 10 students is 28.5.**

questions.question: In a class of 80 students, 40% are girls and the rest are boys. The average weight of the boys is 55.5 kg. If the average weight of all the students in the class is 54 kg, then the average weight (in kg) of the girls is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Ratio of number of boys to girls is 3:2

By Mixture and Allegation method

**Given:**

Total students = 80 

Average weight of boys = 55.5 kg

Average weight of class = 54 kg

**Formula used:**

Average = Sum of all the terms/Total number of terms

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

⇒ Number of girls = 40% × 80 = 32

⇒ Number of boys = 60% × 80 = 48

Sum of weight of class = 54 × 80 = 4320 kg 

Sum of weight of boys = 55.5 × 48 = 2664 kg

⇒ Sum of weight of girls = 4320 - 2664 

⇒ Sum of the weight of girls = 1656 kg 

Average weight of girls = 1656/32 = 51.75 kg

**∴ The average weight of girls is 51.75 kg.**

questions.question: If 30% of (x - y) = 20% of (x + y), then what per cent of x is y ?

questions.question: 36 litres of a mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 5 litres of this mixture is replaced by 5 litres of milk, then find the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

36 liters of a mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1

5 litres of this mixture is replaced by 5 litres of milk

**Calculation:**

Let the quantity of milk and water be 3x and x respectively

⇒ 3x + x = 36

⇒ 4x = 36

⇒ x = 9

In the mixture

⇒ Milk = 3x = 3 × 9 = 27

⇒ Water = x = 9

Quantity of milk removed = 5 × (3/4) = 15/4

⇒ Remaining Milk = 27 - (15/4) = (108 - 15)/4 = 93/4

Quantity of water removed = 5 × (1/4) = 5/4

⇒ Remaining Water = 9 - (5/4) = (36 - 5)/4 = 31/4

New quantity of milk = 93/4 + 5 = (93 + 20)/4 =113/4

Ratio of milk to water in new mixture

⇒ Milk : Water = (113)/(4) : (31)/(4) = 113 : 31

**∴ The ratio of milk to water in the new mixture is 113 : 31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

If we remove 5 litres from 36 litres, remaining mixture will be 31 litres

In 31 litres, the ratio of milk and water will be the same 3:1

Now, 5 litres of milk is added to the mixture

⇒ (3x + 5) + x = 36 ⇒ x = 31/4

Thus, ratio of milk and water is

⇒ (3x + 5) : x = (93/4 + 5) : (31/4)

**∴ The ratio of milk and water in new mixture is 113: 31.**

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 12 times their HCF. If one of the numbers is 15 and the sum of the HCF and LCM is 65, then find the other number.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

LCM = 12 × HCF

LCM + HCF = 65

Number₁ = 15

**Formula Used:**

LCM × HCF = N₁ × N₂

**Calculation:**

12 × HCF + HCF = 65

⇒ 13 × HCF = 65

⇒ HCF = 5

⇒ LCM = 12 × 5 = 60

According to the question,

⇒ 60 × 5 = 15 × N₂ 

⇒ N₂ = 300/15 = 20

**∴ The other number is 20.**

LCM of two or more fractions = (LCM of Numerator)/(HCF of Denominator)

questions.question: A retailer buys a tricycle for ₹1,125. His overhead expenses are ₹75. If he sells the tricycle for ₹1,380, then what is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:

CP = ₹1,125

Overhead Expenses = ₹75

SP = ₹1380

**Formula used:**

Profit % = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100

**Calculation:**

Total CP = 1125 + 75 = ₹1200

⇒ Profit % = [(1380 - 1200)/1200] × 100

⇒ Profit % = (180/1200) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 15%

**∴ The profit percentage is 15%.**

questions.question: A can complete a certain task in 18 days, B in 27 days and C in 36 days. A, B and C began to work together, but A left 4 days before and B left 6 days before the completion of the task. For how many days did B work?
questions.solution:
Given:-

A completes a task in 18 days

B completes a task in 27 days

C completes a task in 36 days

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation: 

Let the work be finished in x days

Let total work be 108 units (LCM of 18, 27,36)

⇒ Efficiency of A = 108/18 = 6 units

⇒ Efficiency of B = 108/27 = 4 units

⇒ Efficiency of C = 108/36 = 3 units

According to the question,

⇒ 6(x - 4) + 4(x - 6) + 3x = 108

⇒ 6x + 4x + 3x - 48 = 108

⇒ 13x = 156

⇒ x = 12 days

B leaves 6 days before completion

⇒ B worked for days = 12 - 6 = 6 days

** ∴ B worked for 6 days.**

questions.question: An article is marked 60% above its cost price. If a profit of 20% is made by selling the article, then what is the discount percentage offered on its marked price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

MP is 60% above its CP

Profit is 20%

**Formula used:**

**1**. MP = CP × (100 + Increase%)/100

**2**. SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100

**3**. Discount% = [(MP - SP)/MP] × 100

**Calculation:**

Let CP of an article be 100

⇒ MP = 100 × (100 + 60)/100 = 160

According to the question,

SP = 100 × (100 + 20)/100 = 120

⇒ Discount% = [(160 - 120)/160] × 100

⇒ Discount% = (40/160) × 100

⇒ Discount% = 25%

**∴ The discount percentage is 25%.**

questions.question: If 45% of a number is equal to two-third of another number, what is the ratio of the first number to the second number?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

45% of a number is equal to two-third of another number

**Calculation:**

Let A and B be the two numbers respectively

⇒ (45/100) × A = (2/3) × B

⇒ A : B = (2 × 100) : (3 × 45)

⇒ A : B = 200 : 135

⇒** **A : B = 40 : 27

**∴ The ratio of the first number to the second number is 40:27.**
